item.title: 'In talks with payment platforms to ensure UPI fee not passed on to consumers': Govt
item.description: The government is currently in talks with payment platforms to ensure that merchant fees do not get passed on to consumers. Starting from October fifteenth, officials will closely monitor this situation to protect consumers. They also reassured that merchants will not incur additional GST costs once the MDR is implemented. This initiative aims to support more domestic players in the market and encourage innovation.
item.dc:creator: SHIVA RAJORA

item.title: Four days after DHS’ ‘Mr Singh’ post, Sikh trucker stabbed in US
item.description: A Sikh truck driver was brutally stabbed seventeen times in Wyoming. This attack occurred just four days after a controversial US government post. Sikh Americans are demanding a full investigation into the assault. They want authorities to determine if hate played a role in the incident. The community fears this incident reflects a concerning climate for them.

item.title: New Green Card rules from September 18: Full list of categories affected
item.description: Effective September 18, the USCIS will enforce new public charge regulations for Green Card applicants. These updated guidelines impose stricter financial evaluations and recognize a broader range of public benefits. This modification impacts family and employment-based Green Card submissions lodged from that date forward. Any applications submitted before September 18, 2026, will adhere to the previous criteria, while some applicant groups will still be exempt from these changes.

item.title: Bangladesh PM Rahman wishes PM Modi on birthday, wishes him good health & high spirit
item.description: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman warmly wished Narendra Modi on his birthday, showcasing Dhaka’s intent to improve its fraught relationship with India. The occasion was marked by messages from various world leaders and leaders from India’s opposition as well. To commemorate, the Bharatiya Janata Party kicked off a series of service activities throughout the month, with well-known figures from the film industry also sharing their best wishes.

item.title: Abhishek Sharma's record 30-ball century powers India to 3-0 T20I series sweep
item.description: Abhishek Sharma's returns in international cricket haven't been the best since the T20I World Cup in March. The runs have come at a premium for him. He wasn't going to let this opportunity re-establish himself as India's undisputed first-choice opener in T20Is even as the buzz around 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi only keeps growing. He finished the series with 209 runs off 85 balls.

item.title: Washington couple spent $300,000 on home plans; state wants 44 acres surrendered
item.description: Tyler Chambers embarked on an ambitious journey to construct his dream home in Washington. Investing nearly $300,000 into regulatory requirements and necessary studies, he was soon met with neighbor complaints that triggered additional demands. These included extensive environmental assessments and a permanent conservation deed restriction on two-thirds of his land. Undeterred by the financial and emotional strain, Chambers remains resolute in his quest to build a home.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Atlantic City’s Steel Pier bought for $4.25m now asks $85 million
item.description: For the eye-catching price of eighty-five million dollars, Atlantic City's Steel Pier, with its storied past, is now on the market. The landmark amusement park provides vast ocean development rights that could lead to exciting future ventures. Purchased by the Catanoso family for just four point two five million fourteen years ago, this beloved destination has the potential for redevelopment into vibrant entertainment or residential facilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Why Mark Zuckerberg's wife's school was shut down despite $125 million in donations,
item.description: Priscilla Chan's Primary School in East Palo Alto has shut down after ten years of operation. The school, backed by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, faced challenges with academic performance. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, leading to the board's unanimous decision to close. While academic results were mixed, the school provided significant well-being and health support for students.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: New Orleans turns 12 million pounds of glass into sand to rebuild wetlands
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative in New Orleans, discarded glass bottles are being turned into sand for coastal restoration. Known as Glass Half Full, this program has successfully redirected millions of pounds of glass from local landfills. Current research is examining the positive impact of this recycled glass sand on the growth and durability of wetland vegetation, providing a creative solution to Louisiana's ongoing coastal land loss issues.

item.description: Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ Texas lakefront mansion is finally complete after years of planning, approvals and construction delays. The couple started designing the home in 2020 and finished it in November 2025. The reported $3 million property includes a private gym, pool, sports court, large kitchen, spa-style bathroom, laundry room and a dedicated space for their dogs.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham’s inspiring journey: How did she rise to WNBA stardom?
item.description: Sophie Elizabeth Cunningham’s inspirational story is a tapestry of athletic versatility, family support, financial hardship and perseverance. Cunningham’s journey from Columbia, Missouri, to the WNBA and the Indiana Fever has been filled with both success and personal trials. Her college record, her professional career, her injuries, her demanding schedule, and her relationship with her fans give a broader view of an athlete whose story is much more than basketball.

item.description: Massachusetts brothers Kirk and Jacob McKinney started Junk Teens in 2021 with a used $4,000 pickup truck while they were still teenagers. What began as junk removal and reselling has grown into a business that generated $3.04 million in revenue from more than 5,500 jobs in 2025. The brothers are now targeting $5 million in revenue in 2026.

item.title: US advances $24.3bn Saudi F-35 deal despite concerns over kingdom's China ties
item.description: The US State Department approved a potential sale of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia. This significant deal is valued at an estimated $24.3 billion for the kingdom. Concerns exist regarding China potentially accessing F-35 technology through Saudi Arabia. The proposed sale also raises questions about Israel's military edge in the region. This approval moves the sale into a more advanced stage of review.

item.title: KBC18: Dowry case survivor from Bilaspur opens up about ‘Agni Kaand’
item.description: On the show Kaun Banega Crorepati, Kapila Taneja bravely shared her traumatic encounter with domestic violence. She described a chilling incident where her in-laws tried to set her ablaze and kept her from her daughter. Surviving this ordeal, which occurred in 2002, required multiple surgeries to treat her injuries. With her winnings of Rs 7,50,000, Taneja aspires to fund her artificial ears and establish a shelter for unwed mothers.

item.title: China asks Iran to rein in Houthis; why Beijing has stepped in now
item.description: China has asked Iran to influence Yemen's Houthis to de-escalate regional tensions. This appeal follows Saudi Arabia's request for Beijing's assistance with Houthi advances. item.title: Meet Tilcayo: Tiny wild cat discovered in Bolivia's forests after more than a century
item.description: Scientists have identified a new wild cat species in Bolivia's cloud forests. This small, slender cat is known locally as Tilcayo and has been formally named. Genetic analysis revealed it is distinct from other known tiger cat species. Local communities have known about this cat for generations, passing down its name. Conservation efforts are needed as its population size remains unknown.
